definition: The forms of Buddhism that developed in Tibet and the Himalaya, including the Nyingma, Kagyu, Sakya and Gelug schools. They combine Indian Buddhist learning with Tibetan monastic, tantric and scholarly traditions.

A living Tibetan religious tradition with its own scriptures, lineages and monasteries. Often described as pre-Buddhist, it has changed over centuries and shares much with Tibetan Buddhism while keeping distinct teachings and rituals.
The personal name of the historical Buddha, a prince of the Shakyas who left home, awakened under the bodhi tree and taught in northern India. Tibetan tradition honours him as the Buddha of this age.

A Buddhist figure of temptation, fear and death, who tries to stop Siddhartha's awakening. Many traditions read Mara symbolically as the forces of craving and self-protection rather than only as a literal being.

An eleventh-century Tibetan yogi and poet of the Kagyu lineage, famous for his cave retreats, his songs and his discipline under Marpa. The Hundred Thousand Songs preserves the tradition attributed to him.

An Indian master of the eighth century, called Guru Rinpoche, whom Tibetan tradition credits with subduing local forces and establishing Buddhism in Tibet. His biographies are legendary and hagiographic.
The primordial buddha of the Bon tradition, whose name means All-Good. He represents the ground of being and the source of Bon's highest teachings, not a creator god who stands outside the world.

A bodhisattva of compassionate action, widely honoured in Tibetan Buddhism. Traditions tell of her arising from Avalokiteshvara's tears or from a princess who vowed to be reborn as a woman to help beings.
The Great Perfection, a teaching on the nature of mind found in the Nyingma school and in Bon. It is transmitted through qualified teachers, and much of its practical instruction is not public.
Coloured cloths printed with prayers and symbols, hung on poles, passes and rooftops in Tibetan regions. The wind is said to carry the blessings and intentions printed on them.
